title: Data graphs: pie charts and line graphs
subject: math

objectives.text: Read a pie chart as fractions of a whole and read values and trends from a line graph
successCriteria: I can say 6 of 12 pupils chose apples (1/2), and 3 each chose bananas and grapes (1/4 each)
I can read plants sold as Jan 20, Feb 35, Mar 30 and Apr 50 and spot the dip in March
assessmentPoints: Pie chart answers in the opening activity
Responses when the steeper-line trap is sprung in the fourth activity

objectives.text: Compare two bars of data by subtracting their heights and check the axis scale before comparing how steep two lines look
successCriteria: I can read soccer 13 and badminton 8 and work out 13 - 8 = 5 more chose soccer
I can check that both shops rose from 20 to 40 even though graph B looks flatter on its 0 to 200 axis
assessmentPoints: Bar comparison answers in the third activity
Worksheet answers in the closing practice

activities.title: Reading a pie chart: who likes what?
Reading a line graph: a rising trend
Worked example: comparing two bars of data

differentiation.support: Provide the two bar heights labelled 13 and 8 so learners can follow the subtraction before reading heights themselves.

differentiation.stretch: Ask learners to explain why a line that looks steeper has not necessarily risen by more.
